introduction: “The Greatest Name should be found upon the lips in the first awaking moment of early dawn.” The readings pass from that daily habit to the meanings found in a word, to the claim that the Name hidden through the ages has appeared in a Person, and then to dozens of prayers that begin “I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great Name” and to calls to arise in its strength. The reverence for a divine name is among the oldest things in religion. Moses asks the name and hears “I AM THAT I AM”; the psalmist runs into the name as into a tower; the Lord’s Prayer begins by hallowing it; Paul speaks of a name above every name; the Qur’an says that His are the most beautiful names and that hearts find rest in remembrance. The same sources set the cautions: a name not to be taken in vain, a name refused to Manoah, wonders done “in thy name” by those never known, repetitions that are vain. Lao-tzu doubts that any name is the enduring one, and Juliet that a name matters at all.
questions: Moses is given a name at the bush and Manoah is refused one. What do the readings mean by a Name that was hidden and is now manifest?

“Unto whichsoever ye cry, it is the same. His are the most beautiful names.” Reading 22 says the Promised One is named differently in each Book. Is the Greatest Name one name among these, or something else?
Peter says there is “none other name”. How might a Christian and a Bahá’í each read that sentence in the light of reading 22?
Jesus warns of those who did wonders in his name and of vain repetitions. What in the readings distinguishes invocation from the use of a name as a charm?
David goes out “in the name of the Lord of hosts”. How do the last readings connect the remembrance of a Name with steadfast action?

outside.why: The Greatest Name “should be found upon the lips in the first awaking moment of early dawn”. My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O Lord; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.
From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the Lord’s name is to be praised.
“Constant use in daily invocation.” The Qur’an: O ye who believe! Remember God with much remembrance, and glorify Him early and late.
“There lie glorious meanings in the word.” Plato’s Socrates holds that a name is an instrument of teaching and of distinguishing natures, as a shuttle is of distinguishing the threads of the web.
Call on the Name when you wish the soul’s palate sweetened. Thy name is as ointment poured forth.
“The cry of the Concourse on high” is a name of God. Isaiah heard the seraphim cry one to another: Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts.
The greeting is itself the blessed word. The Qur’an on greetings: when ye are greeted with a greeting, greet ye with a better than it or return it.
What is available now is the meaning of two letters only. For we know in part, and we prophesy in part.
Lao-tzu begins: the name that can be named is not the enduring and unchanging name. The readings revere a Name; he distrusts every name. Does a “Greatest Name” answer him or fall under his sentence?
The reading interprets this verse: the mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks.
The Name has aspects: belief in God, in the Prophet, in the witnesses. Israel’s confession begins with a name and a number: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord.
Praise beyond what all things can attain. Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory.
“Mentioned in every Book by a different name.” Zechariah: in that day shall there be one Lord, and his name one.
The Qur’an: cry unto God, or cry unto the Beneficent; unto whichsoever ye cry, it is the same. His are the most beautiful names.
Juliet: what’s in a name? That which we call a rose by any other name would smell as sweet. If the Promised One is named differently in every Book, how much weight can any one name bear?
The Name promised in the Books has appeared. His name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
The mention of the Name “must be at the beginning, for it precedes”. In the beginning was the Word.
The Name that adorns the preamble of the Tablet of Eternity. Moses asks what name he shall give, and hears: I AM THAT I AM.
The Most Great Name “was hidden in the eternity of eternities”. The mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest.

Manoah asks the messenger his name and is refused: why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is secret? Scripture guards the name as often as it gives it. What changes when a hidden name is spoken?
The Name is bidden to come forth from silence. Jesus in his last prayer: I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me.
“The Lord of Eternity hath come with the Most Great Name.” God hath given him a name which is above every name: that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.

The peoples are summoned by this Name. Peter: there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved. Each community has its one name. How do the readings understand the others?
The horizon is illumined, “yet most of the people perceive not”. The light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
The world is adorned and people remain heedless. He was in the world, and the world knew him not.
A banner raised: blessed is he who hastens to it. The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe.
“The whole world was created for this blessed Day.” This is the day which the Lord hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

Through the Name “the peoples were scattered and the sincere ones were gathered”. Simeon: this child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and for a sign which shall be spoken against.
Take hold of the Name and cast aside what the peoples possess. Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the Lord our God.
The choice wine “whose seal We have broken”. The Qur’an’s righteous are given to drink of a pure wine, sealed, whose seal is musk.
The key of the Name opens the gates of bounty. I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven.
“The Greatest Name that brings the dead to life.” Peter to the lame man at the gate: in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.
Be confident in the influence of the Name. Many will say, Lord, Lord, have we not in thy name done many wonderful works? and hear: I never knew you. What must go with the use of a holy name?
“O Physician of troubled hearts!” Is there no balm in Gilead; is there no physician there?
Use of the Name causes the soul to “step forth freed, reborn”. Be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.
Its effects reach soul and conscience, bone and flesh. Verily in the remembrance of God do hearts find rest.
Believers ask for stones engraved with the Name. To him that overcometh will I give a white stone, and in the stone a new name written.

A woman cries out with joy at the Name impressed on a stone. Israel was commanded not to take the name of the Lord in vain, and came to avoid pronouncing it at all. Between wearing a name and never uttering it, where does reverence lie?
He sat by a sick child, took its hand and said the Greatest Name. Let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: and the prayer of faith shall save the sick.
“I invoke Thee by Thy Most Great Name.” Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you.
A prayer made “by” the Name. The Lord’s Prayer begins with it: hallowed be thy name.
Petition after petition opens “I beseech Thee by Thy Most Great Name”. Jesus: use not vain repetitions; your Father knoweth what things ye have need of. What makes an invocation more than a formula?
A child “clinging to … Thy Most Great Name”. Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine.
The Name through which the heaven was cleft. The rider of the Apocalypse had a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.
Hearts were shaken, save those who heard and said “Here am I”. Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth.
“Remind the people of this Most Great Name.” From the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles.
He speaks through the Name so that the clamour of the heedless does not silence him. They spake the word of God with boldness.
“Through the power of the Most Great Name … arise to action.” David to Goliath: thou comest to me with a sword and a spear; but I come to thee in the name of the Lord of hosts.
Manifest supreme steadfastness. Be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord.
“Seek thou shelter in the Greatest Name.” He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.

The effect of all names depends on the Most Great. Micah’s age of peace has all people walking every one in the name of his god, “and we will walk in the name of the Lord our God”. How do a sovereign Name and many names live together?

shortfall: Most of the readings are single sentences that announce the appearance of the Most Great Name or open a petition with it; companions were given to the kinds of statement (invocation at dawn, hidden and manifest, healing, shelter, action) and not to each.
